domain.name: Game & 3D Production
domain.description: Practical 3D modeling, UVs, materials, lighting, animation, engine integration, optimization, world building, and asset-pipeline fundamentals.

competencies.name: 3D Modeling & Topology
competencies.description: Build efficient forms with topology suited to the asset's purpose.
competencies.purpose: Create assets that hold shape, deform when needed, and remain manageable downstream.

units.title: Topology should serve the use case
units.content: A hero character, static building, background prop, and simulation mesh have different topology needs; clean topology is functional, not decorative.

units.title: Modeling workflow
units.content: Define scale and silhouette; block major forms; establish proportions; add secondary forms; refine topology around deformation or shading needs; check normals and transforms; then create detail only where it survives the target view.

units.title: Modeling failures
units.content: Avoid adding density before proportions are correct, inconsistent scale, nonmanifold geometry without reason, hidden duplicate faces, and topology that creates shading or deformation artifacts.

drills.title: Model a game-ready prop
drills.prompt: Plan a game-ready street prop from reference through blockout, topology, detail, and export.

competencies.name: UV Mapping & Texturing
competencies.description: Create efficient UV layouts and textures that support consistent detail and material response.
competencies.purpose: Make surfaces readable without wasting texture memory.

units.title: UV workflow
units.content: Apply scale; identify logical seams; unwrap; minimize distortion; keep texel density intentional; pack islands with padding; then test with a checker before painting or baking.

units.title: Texture resolution is a budget
units.content: Texel density should reflect screen importance, repetition, asset size, and memory limits instead of maximizing every texture.

units.title: UV and texture failures
units.content: Avoid overlapping unique UVs unintentionally, inconsistent texel density, insufficient padding, painting before checking distortion, and excessive unique textures for repeated surfaces.

drills.title: Plan UVs for a modular building
drills.prompt: Design a UV and material strategy for a modular brick building set with repeated walls, trim, doors, and hero signage.

competencies.name: Materials & Shading
competencies.description: Build physically coherent materials using surface properties, masks, and reusable shader logic.
competencies.purpose: Create believable and controllable surfaces across assets.

units.title: Material response describes surface behavior
units.content: Base color, roughness, metallic response, normal detail, opacity, and emission should represent the surface rather than compensate for lighting mistakes.

units.title: Material build order
units.content: Identify real surface behavior; establish base values; add large-scale variation; add wear only where plausible; use masks for reusable variation; test under neutral and scene lighting; then optimize shader complexity.

units.title: Material failures
units.content: Avoid baked lighting in base color, random edge wear everywhere, extreme roughness values without reference, and unique shaders when parameterized shared materials would work.

drills.title: Build a street material set
drills.prompt: Define materials for asphalt, concrete, painted metal, glass, and weathered brick with reusable parameters.

competencies.name: 3D Lighting & Rendering
competencies.description: Use light, exposure, color, and atmosphere to communicate form, mood, and hierarchy.
competencies.purpose: Make scenes readable and emotionally intentional.

units.title: Lighting has both physical and storytelling jobs
units.content: Lighting should explain form and spatial relationships while also guiding attention and mood; more lights do not automatically create better lighting.

units.title: Scene lighting workflow
units.content: Choose time, mood, and focal point; establish broad environment or key light; set exposure; add fill or practicals only for specific needs; control contrast and color; then test focal hierarchy from target cameras.

units.title: Lighting failures
units.content: Avoid fixing exposure with dozens of local lights, inconsistent light direction, crushed values that hide gameplay/readability, and dramatic fog that destroys depth cues.

drills.title: Light a night street scene
drills.prompt: Plan lighting for a playable urban street at night with readable navigation and a strong focal storefront.

competencies.name: Rigging & Animation Fundamentals
competencies.description: Prepare and animate objects or characters with usable controls, timing, and deformation.
competencies.purpose: Create motion that reads clearly and survives engine integration.

units.title: Animation communicates through timing, spacing, and clear poses
units.content: Even technically correct motion feels weak when poses are ambiguous, spacing is even without intention, or the action lacks anticipation and follow-through.

units.title: Animation blocking workflow
units.content: Confirm rig and scale; block key poses and contacts; establish timing; refine arcs and spacing; add overlap and secondary motion; inspect deformation; then export with consistent root and frame conventions.

units.title: Animation failures
units.content: Avoid polishing before timing works, foot sliding, uncontrolled root motion, inconsistent frame rates, and rigs with unclear constraints or transform spaces.

drills.title: Block an interaction animation
drills.prompt: Plan a character reaching for, opening, and releasing a door with clear contact points and engine-ready root behavior.

competencies.name: Game Engine Asset Integration
competencies.description: Move assets into an engine with correct scale, pivots, collision, materials, LODs, and naming.
competencies.purpose: Make art assets function correctly in the runtime environment.

units.title: Asset integration checklist
units.content: Freeze or apply required transforms; verify unit scale and pivot; export supported formats; import with naming rules; assign materials; create or validate collision; configure LOD or streaming behavior; test under runtime lighting and interaction.

units.title: Validate in engine early
units.content: An asset that looks correct in the DCC can still fail because of scale, normals, materials, collision, or performance; test before producing many variants.

units.title: Integration failures
units.content: Avoid inconsistent pivots, collision more complex than the visible mesh without reason, unbounded material slots, and discovering unit-scale errors after a whole environment is assembled.

drills.title: Integrate a modular environment kit
drills.prompt: Define the import and validation rules for a modular street kit used repeatedly in an engine.

competencies.name: Real-Time Performance Optimization
competencies.description: Balance visual quality against CPU, GPU, memory, draw-call, and streaming budgets.
competencies.purpose: Keep scenes performant without blindly reducing quality.

units.title: Optimize measured bottlenecks
units.content: Geometry, materials, lighting, shadows, overdraw, texture memory, physics, scripts, and streaming stress different resources; optimization should follow profiling evidence.

units.title: Optimization loop
units.content: Define target hardware and performance budget; profile representative scenes; identify the largest bottleneck; change one major cost source; compare before/after; protect visual priorities; repeat until target is met.

units.title: Optimization failures
units.content: Avoid optimizing in an empty test scene, reducing polygon count when shader cost is dominant, disabling quality globally instead of fixing hotspots, and judging performance from editor view alone.

drills.title: Optimize a city block
drills.prompt: A city block misses frame target only when looking down a long street. Build a profiling and optimization plan.

competencies.name: World Building & Asset Pipeline
competencies.description: Organize environments into reusable modules, references, source assets, versions, and production rules.
competencies.purpose: Scale 3D world production without losing consistency or provenance.

units.title: World pipeline design
units.content: Define coordinate and scale conventions; separate source, intermediate, and runtime assets; create modular kits; establish naming and version rules; preserve reference provenance; validate automated exports; document handoff and rollback.

units.title: Reuse structure before duplicating detail
units.content: Large worlds scale through repeatable kits, procedural rules, instances, and data-driven placement while hero areas receive selective bespoke detail.

units.title: Pipeline failures
units.content: Avoid one giant unversioned scene, duplicated materials and meshes with no source link, destructive exports overwriting source assets, and inconsistent coordinate conventions between tools.

drills.title: Design a neighborhood production pipeline
drills.prompt: Create a Blender-to-engine pipeline for a real-world neighborhood using GIS/reference data, modular buildings, hero assets, and versioned exports.
